reconcile.connective: Commentators read the two texts as answering different questions: Matthew 6 gives prayer's pattern; Romans 8:26 concerns not knowing what specifically to ask for.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the two texts as flatly opposed: Jesus teaches a prayer, yet Paul says believers don't know what to pray for.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Do Christians know how to pray?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Do Christians know how to pray?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/pray.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Because we know not what to pray for as we ought, he here helps our infirmities, by putting words into our mouths; after this manner therefore pray ye, Mat 6:9.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Henry explicitly grounds the giving of the Lord's Prayer in the very ignorance Romans 8:26 names, making Matt 6:9 the answer to Paul's statement rather than a rival claim.

excerpts.excerpt_text: but what they are ignorant of is chiefly the matter of prayer: indeed the whole Bible is an instruction in general to this work, so is the prayer Christ taught his disciples, and the several prayers of saints recorded in the Scriptures; the promises of God, and their own wants and necessities, may, and do, greatly direct them; … but what of all things they seem to be, at least at some times, at a loss about, is what to pray for with respect to things temporal, such as riches, honour, friends …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill distinguishes the general instruction in prayer (which he says the Lord's Prayer supplies) from the specific 'matter' of temporal particulars believers still lack, directly reconciling the two texts.

excerpts.excerpt_text: It is not the proper matter of prayer that believers are at so much loss about, for the fullest directions are given them on this head: but to ask for the right things "as they ought" is the difficulty.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB states plainly that believers are not ignorant of the content of prayer, since 'the fullest directions' (including the Lord's Prayer) are given; the difficulty is asking rightly amid spiritual dimness, not not knowing what to pray for.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-14), on Matthew 6:9
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry ties Matt 6:9 directly to the Romans 8:26 language ('we know not what to pray for as we ought'), reading the Lord's Prayer as Christ's provision for that very infirmity — already surfaced as MHC/40/6/9 on this row; Haley's Alleged Discrepancies does not treat this specific pairing.
